[2] "issue-151" section 2:
> **Blocked:** The Danish exhaustion sentence waits for a Danish speaker's sign-off (KU-15), and the release gate that must fail while its verdicts are unset (FR-029) belongs to #25, itself blocked on KU-03 and KU-07.
>
> **When unblocked:** besides this issue's criteria, add `tool_budget_exhausted` to the exhaustiveness fixture `apps/api/test/fixtures/escalationTriggers.ts` (added by #275), or `npm run typecheck` fails, and drop the "Unmet for `tool_budget_exhausted`" marker from FR-002 in `specs/support-agent-escalation/spec.md`. Two findings from a first build: HAL Engine passes `requestedTools` as the raw tool names the model asked for, so log only registered names (mask the rest) and allowlist `requestedTools` in `apps/api/src/shared/logger.ts`; and the fragment needs the turn's recorder and logger, so it is a factory like `createEscalationHooks`, not a constant.

[3] "issue-151" section 3:
## Why

`094` ships an `onToolBudgetExhausted` hook but deliberately writes no words - Danish belongs to the consumer, not the engine. With no consumer installed, an exhausted budget ends a turn on whatever text the last provider call produced, which on a round spent entirely requesting tools is nothing. The customer asks a question, watches the typing stop, and reads an empty bubble. Nothing else in the backlog owns this sentence: `049` owns the budget itself, `051`'s system prompt is instructions the model never sees at this point, and `117`'s Danish failure catalogue renders on the `error` frame while an exhausted budget is a `stream_end`.

## What to do

In `re-cinq/Otto`, `apps/api` only:

[4] "issue-151" section 4:
## What to do

- `apps/api/src/budget/budgetMessage.ts` (new): exports `TOOL_BUDGET_MESSAGE_DA`, a single Danish string constant that promises nothing concrete (no channel, time, or person) and carries no persona name.
- `apps/api/src/budget/budgetHooks.ts` (new): exports `budgetHooks: Partial<OrchestratorHooks>`, whose `onToolBudgetExhausted` fragment calls `escalationRecorder.mark(session.sessionId, 'tool_budget_exhausted')` then returns `TOOL_BUDGET_MESSAGE_DA`. The string renders in the assistant's own bubble (via the normal `entry_upsert` → `entry_delta` → `entry_commit` text path), not through `117`'s catalogue - it is first person, the opposite of `117`'s impersonal wording, because it appears to speak as the assistant rather than as a system alert.
- `apps/api/src/escalation/triggers.ts`: `EscalationTrigger` gains a sixth member, `tool_budget_exhausted`.
- `apps/api/src/hooks/hookKinds.ts` and `composeHooks.ts`: register `onToolBudgetExhausted: 'firstOrSkip'` - a chain that awaits fragments in order and returns the first non-empty string; a fragment that throws is logged and skipped rather than aborting the turn.

[5] "issue-151" section 5:
## What to do

- `apps/api/src/start-server.ts`: wire the fragment as a fourth entry inside the existing single `composeHooks([...])` array.
- `docs/danish-review.md`: add one row for the new string, verdicts unset.

[6] "issue-151" section 6:
## What to do

Log `requestedTools` (tool names only, never `toolInput`) at `warn` alongside `sessionId` and `maxToolRounds` - this is diagnostic-only and never persisted to the escalation document.

[7] "issue-151" section 7:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `budgetMessage.ts` exports `TOOL_BUDGET_MESSAGE_DA` as a non-empty string with no `<` character and no digit
- [ ] `budgetHooks.ts` exports `budgetHooks: Partial<OrchestratorHooks>` whose only key is `onToolBudgetExhausted`, typed against `OrchestratorHooks` from `@re-cinq/hal-engine`, with no `any`
- [ ] The fragment calls `escalationRecorder.mark(session.sessionId, 'tool_budget_exhausted')` exactly once before returning `TOOL_BUDGET_MESSAGE_DA`
- [ ] `EscalationTrigger` gains `tool_budget_exhausted` as a sixth member, and `054`'s exhaustiveness `switch` (no `default`) is updated in this PR
- [ ] A full engine run with `maxToolRounds: 2` and a stub that always requests tools produces exactly one document in the `escalations` collection whose `trigger`/`triggers` contains `tool_budget_exhausted`
- [ ] A turn where a TMS call returned `503` **and** the budget then exhausted produces exactly **one** document whose `triggers` array contains both `tms_unavailable` and `tool_budget_exhausted` (dedup across two trigger sources in one turn)

[8] "issue-151" section 8:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A conversation that ends normally (`tool_use` then `end_turn`) writes no escalation record and calls the fragment zero times
- [ ] `HOOK_KINDS` gains `onToolBudgetExhausted: 'firstOrSkip'` and still compiles as `satisfies Record<keyof OrchestratorHooks, HookKind>` against the bumped `@re-cinq/hal-engine`
- [ ] `composeHooks` supports a `firstOrSkip` chain: two fragments returning `'a'` and `'b'` yield `'a'`; a first fragment returning `undefined` or `''` yields `'b'`; all fragments returning `undefined` yields `undefined`
- [ ] **NIS-2 Article 21 operational resilience.** A fragment whose `onToolBudgetExhausted` rejects does not fail the turn: the next fragment still runs, the terminal frame is `stream_end` (never `error`), and exactly one `log.error` is emitted
- [ ] `start-server.ts` passes a fourth named fragment (`budget`) inside the single `composeHooks([...])` array literal; no object literal or spread reaches `orchestrator.hooks` outside it

[9] "issue-151" section 9:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **GDPR.** The `warn` log line carries exactly `sessionId`, `maxToolRounds`, and `requestedTools` (tool names only) and nothing else - a test with a user message containing a name and phone number and a tool input containing a booking reference asserts neither appears in any logged argument, and no key named `toolInput` appears
- [ ] **GDPR.** `054`'s five-field `toEqual` assertion over the whole escalation document still passes with this trigger, confirming `requestedTools` never reaches the collection
- [ ] The string is Danish, promises nothing (no phone number, email, opening hour, or the words `ring`, `minutter`, `timer`), and carries no persona name
- [ ] **EU AI Act.** The exhausted-turn string adds no claim to be a person - `062`'s `AI_TERMS` check applied in the negative (Article 50(1))
- [ ] `docs/danish-review.md` gains one row for `TOOL_BUDGET_MESSAGE_DA` with `language`/`register` verdicts unset and the proposer named; `055`'s release gate fails while unset
- [ ] The spec states in one sentence that a rendered sentence means the customer was told, not that a human was notified

[10] "issue-151" section 10:

[3] "issue-151" section 3:
## Why

`094` ships an `onToolBudgetExhausted` hook but deliberately writes no words - Danish belongs to the consumer, not the engine. With no consumer installed, an exhausted budget ends a turn on whatever text the last provider call produced, which on a round spent entirely requesting tools is nothing. The customer asks a question, watches the typing stop, and reads an empty bubble. Nothing else in the backlog owns this sentence: `049` owns the budget itself, `051`'s system prompt is instructions the model never sees at this point, and `117`'s Danish failure catalogue renders on the `error` frame while an exhausted budget is a `stream_end`.
